articles.title: URGENT: Police appeal to find missing 10-year-old Rayah in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Greater Manchester Police has launched an urgent appeal to find 10-year-old Rayah, who was last seen on Bower Avenue in Rochdale at around 8.30am today.
articles.content_html:
Greater Manchester Police has launched an urgent appeal to find 10-year-old Rayah, who has been missing from Rochdale since this morning.

Rayah was last seen on Bower Avenue in Rochdale at around 8.30am on Friday 14 August. Police say officers are becoming increasingly concerned about her and want to make sure she is safe and well.

The police appeal describes Rayah as a child with olive or tanned skin, approximately 4ft 5in tall, with mousey brown curly hair worn in a ponytail.

She was last seen wearing purple and white striped bottoms, a T-shirt and a denim jacket. She was also carrying a backpack and had a remote-control car with her.

Anyone who sees Rayah, knows where she may be, or has information which could help officers locate her is urged to contact Greater Manchester Police on 0161 856 1367, quoting reference MSP/06PP/0001322/26.

Always call 999 in an emergency.

Rochdale Daily will update this appeal as soon as further verified information is released by police.

articles.title: Tram Services Suspended Between Oldham Mumps and Rochdale Town Centre from 17 to 28 August 2026
articles.excerpt: No trams will operate between Oldham Mumps and Rochdale Town Centre from 17 to 28 August 2026 due to essential repair work at Derker following a landslip in 2024.
articles.content_html:
From 17 to 28 August 2026, tram services will be suspended between Oldham Mumps and Rochdale Town Centre. This disruption is necessary for engineers to complete the next phase of repair work at Derker, which was affected by a landslip in 2024.

The repair work aims to address the structural issues caused by the landslip and is part of ongoing efforts to ensure the safety and reliability of tram services. Once the repairs are completed, the temporary speed restrictions currently in place will be lifted.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly during this period, as alternative transport arrangements may be required. The tram operator has not yet provided details on replacement services or diversions.

Further updates will be available on the tram operator's website as the work progresses, and passengers are encouraged to check for the latest information regarding service changes and the expected resumption of normal operations.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Netball launched as Rochdale Netball Club joins Dale family
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Netball Club is becoming Rochdale AFC Netball in a new partnership with Rochdale AFC and its Community Trust, bringing nearly 200 weekly players into the club's wider sporting family.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Netball Club is joining the Rochdale AFC family under a new identity as Rochdale AFC Netball, in a partnership designed to grow the sport and create more opportunities for women, girls and the wider community across the borough.

The agreement brings together Rochdale AFC, Rochdale AFC Community Trust and one of the borough's established community sports clubs under the wider 'Our Teams' banner.

Rochdale Netball Club currently runs teams from under-six level through to seniors, with nearly 200 players taking to the court each week. Under the new Rochdale AFC Netball identity, the organisations hope to strengthen the route from school participation into junior and adult club netball while also expanding opportunities in coaching, volunteering and leadership.

The partnership is expected to support new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing and volunteer development. The shared Rochdale AFC identity could also open up additional opportunities for sponsorship, commercial support, community events and promotion through the football club.

Amy Williams, Chair of Rochdale AFC Netball, described the move as a fantastic opportunity for both the club and the sport locally, saying joining the Rochdale AFC family would provide a stronger platform to grow the game and inspire more women and girls to become involved.

Rochdale AFC chief executive Laura Thomas, herself a former netball player, said she was thrilled to welcome the club into the wider Rochdale AFC family and stressed that the club's ambition to build a thriving community extends beyond football.

Ryan Bradley, Community Director at Rochdale AFC Community Trust, said the football club, charity and netball club shared common values and could combine their respective strengths. He said bringing the organisations together under one brand would raise netball's profile in Rochdale and strengthen support for volunteers, coaches, community outreach and school work.

Rochdale AFC Netball will be based at Edgar Wood. The Community Trust also pointed to plans for the Community Football and Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee, saying the geographical proximity of the projects made closer cooperation a natural step.

The move follows a wider trend in British sport in which professional football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to increase visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the organisations say their approach will remain community focused and open to people of all ages.

Further information about Rochdale AFC Netball teams, programmes and opportunities to get involved is expected to be announced in due course.

articles.title: Rochdale businesses urged to back Denehurst House in £30-a-month veterans challenge
articles.excerpt: A Rochdale veterans support organisation is asking 100 local businesses to pledge £30 a month to help keep Denehurst House operational and support former service personnel in need.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale veterans support organisation has launched a drive to recruit 100 local businesses willing to pledge £30 a month towards keeping Denehurst House operational.

Get Together After Serving CIC, which is behind the campaign, says Denehurst House provides support for veterans including emergency housing, hot meals and mental health support. The organisation is promoting the appeal as the Rochdale 100 Businesses Challenge and is asking firms across the borough to make a regular monthly contribution.

If all 100 places are filled, the campaign would generate £3,000 each month in pledged support, equivalent to £36,000 over a full year if every business remained involved for 12 months. The appeal describes the contribution as a relatively small commitment for an individual business which, collectively, could make a significant difference to the service.

Campaign material highlights community spirit, warm meals and local businesses working together, with the message: 'Together, we keep Denehurst House operational.' It also says the project aims to provide a lifeline to veterans when they need it most.

The initiative is seeking support from companies of all sizes rather than relying on a handful of major donors. That model would spread the cost across the local business community while giving Denehurst House a more predictable stream of recurring income.

Local businesses interested in joining the challenge are being asked to contact Get Together After Serving CIC by emailing hello@gtascic.co.uk.

Rochdale Daily is publishing the appeal as today's front-page community story to help local firms understand what is being requested, how the funding model works and how they can take part.

articles.title: Service Changes on Rochdale Line Due to Planned Works
articles.excerpt: Planned works on the Rochdale line will result in service changes this weekend, with further disruptions expected until 28 August. Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has announced that planned works will affect services on the Rochdale line this weekend, specifically on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August. These works are part of ongoing improvements in the city centre and along the Rochdale line, which will continue until Friday 28 August.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys in advance, as these changes may impact travel times and service availability. TfGM has not specified the exact nature of the service changes, but they are likely to affect both tram and train services along the line.

In addition to the Rochdale line works, there are also ongoing issues at several tram stops. The lifts at Failsworth and Etihad Campus tram stops are currently out of service, meaning there is no step-free access available. Passengers needing step-free access are advised to travel to Hollinwood or Velopark tram stops instead. For assistance, customers can contact the Metrolink customer service centre at 0161 244 1000.

Passengers are encouraged to check the TfGM travel alerts page for the latest updates and further information regarding the planned works and any other service disruptions. The contact centre is available from 7am to 8pm on weekdays and from 8am to 8pm on weekends and bank holidays.

articles.title: Rochdale businesses urged to back Denehurst House in £30-a-month veterans challenge
articles.excerpt: Get Together After Serving CIC is calling on 100 local businesses to pledge £30 a month to help keep Denehurst House operational and support veterans in need.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale veterans organisation has launched a drive to recruit 100 local businesses willing to contribute £30 a month towards the running of Denehurst House.

Get Together After Serving CIC, known as GTAS CIC, is promoting the Rochdale 100-Businesses Challenge as a way for firms across the borough to make a relatively small regular contribution which, collectively, could provide significant ongoing support.

Campaign material shared with Rochdale Daily says Denehurst House provides support for veterans including emergency housing, hot meals, company and mental-health support. The organisation describes the building as a lifeline for former service personnel at times when they may be facing isolation, housing difficulties or other pressures.

The campaign is asking for 100 businesses to pledge £30 each month. If all 100 places are filled, that would amount to £3,000 a month in regular support for the project, or £36,000 over a full year if every pledge remained in place.

GTAS CIC says the purpose of the challenge is not simply to raise money, but to create a lasting partnership between local employers, traders and the veterans community. Its campaign artwork highlights volunteering, shared meals and local business involvement under the message that stronger community links can create a real impact.

Denehurst House is presented by the organisation as a base where veterans can find practical help as well as human contact. The campaign stresses the value of warm meals and company alongside emergency accommodation and mental-health support, reflecting the reality that a person in crisis may need several forms of help at the same time.

For businesses, the proposition is deliberately simple: £30 a month, with the combined backing of 100 companies intended to provide a more predictable stream of funding than one-off donations alone. That regularity can be particularly important for community organisations which have to meet continuing costs while responding to people whose needs cannot always be predicted in advance.

The challenge also gives Rochdale firms an opportunity to support a project rooted in the borough and aimed specifically at people who have served in the Armed Forces. GTAS CIC's message to businesses is that even a modest individual contribution can become substantial when it is repeated across a large local network.

The organisation is now seeking companies of all sizes to take part. Businesses interested in joining the Rochdale 100-Businesses Challenge are being asked to contact GTAS CIC by email at hello@gtascic.co.uk.

articles.title: Police No Longer Treat Death of Woman Found at Milnrow Farm as Murder
articles.excerpt: Police have confirmed that they are no longer treating the death of a woman discovered after a fire at Higher Tunshill Farm in Milnrow as a murder investigation. Emergency services responded to the incident on July 3.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

18:42, 14 August 2026

Police have confirmed that the death of a woman discovered following a fire at Higher Tunshill Farm in Milnrow is no longer being treated as a murder investigation. Emergency services were called to the scene on July 3.

20:30, 13 August 2026

Police have confirmed that they are no longer treating the death of a woman discovered after a fire at Higher Tunshill Farm in Milnrow as a murder investigation. Emergency services responded to the incident on July 3.

Police have announced that they are no longer treating the death of a woman found following a fire at Higher Tunshill Farm in Milnrow as a murder investigation. The incident occurred at approximately 12.30pm on Friday, July 3, when emergency services were called to reports of a fire at the farm.

Upon arrival, emergency responders discovered the body of a woman. Following an initial investigation, detectives have stated that there is no third-party involvement in her death, leading to the conclusion that it is not being treated as a homicide.

The fire at the farm prompted a significant emergency response, with multiple units dispatched to the scene. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the fire and the woman's death is ongoing, but police have reassured the public that there is no immediate threat to safety.

Authorities have not released the identity of the woman or further details regarding the cause of the fire. Updates will be provided as the investigation progresses.
